title: Why Theo's Lifetime ISA Cost Him £6,250 😬
description:
Nora and Theo both paid £20,000 into a Lifetime ISA (£4,000 a year for 5 years) and both got the 25% government bonus, so each pot hit £25,000. Nora bought a £320,000 first flat and kept every penny. Theo fell for a £480,000 flat, £30,000 over the £450,000 first-home limit, so his withdrawal paid the 25% charge on the whole pot: £6,250 gone, £18,750 back. That's £1,250 less than he put in.

The 25% bonus is on what you pay in; the 25% charge is on everything, bonus included. Know the price cap before you start viewing.

Would you have spotted the limit? Nora or Theo? 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration only: both pay £4,000/yr for 5 years; cash only, interest and investment returns ignored. Lifetime ISA rules from GOV.UK (checked Oct 2026): open before 40, pay in up to £4,000 a year, 25% government bonus (max £1,000/yr); a first home must cost £450,000 or less, be bought with a mortgage and at least 12 months after your first payment; other withdrawals pay a 25% charge. The government has consulted on replacing the Lifetime ISA, so rules may change. Source: GOV.UK (gov.uk/lifetime-isa). This is not financial advice.
